page: UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-128GB is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on KVM virtualization within the UpCloud Premium product tier. It features 64 x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores using the AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at a base speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, backed by vector instruction support spanning AVX, AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16), and AVX-VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server is configured with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and is provisioned with 500 GB of local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark testing reflects exceptional parallel processing power. Multi-core evaluations place the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,065, a PassMark CPU score of 89,600.48, and a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 132,481.25. Workloads involving code compilation via Clang (63,829) and ray tracing (101,430) also rank in the top decile. In single-core operations, the server delivers strong to top-tier throughput, recording 2,550 in Geekbench and 2,860.16 in stress-ng. Conversely, large-block uncached memory operations and PassMark memory benchmarks fall into the middle 50 percent category, and small-model CPU LLM inference shows low efficiency.

Given its compute-heavy resource density, UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-128GB is well suited for CPU-bound tasks that demand high core concurrency without extreme per-core memory requirements. Practical deployments include distributed compilation, continuous integration and build pipelines, CPU-based rendering, compression pipelines, and static web serving, supported by bundled high-speed SSD capacity.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-64xCPU-128GB is a high-density, compute-oriented instance powered by KVM virtualization. Driven by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, the configuration delivers 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 128 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per vCPU, 500 GB of integrated local SSD storage, and one public IPv4 address, with no hardware GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by top 10 percent scores in Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Clang compilation tests. Single-core compute and cryptographic processing also achieve upper-quartile results, while memory bandwidth remains within average ranges. This instance is best aligned with compute-intensive parallel workloads such as continuous integration build clusters, parallel data compression, ray tracing, and high-throughput static web serving.
